course: Projects were quite intense but through the end of the course I understood better that all of them eventually had a constructive purpose in the way of thesis.

The assignments were enjoyable and definitely moved me forward in my practice. The topics were inspiring and the weekly workload was appropriate. The main thing that was negative is that I found the number and distribution of the projects mostly flawed. I think, at the graduate level, the projects could have been much heavier content-wise. There could have been fewer assignments so that they could have required more time and the resulting work would have been much more polished and finalized. The requirements could have been a little more open so that each student could have produced work that was more fitting to their career and academic goals. I would suggest that the syllabus would be much more fitting to a graduate student if it had consisted of one or two main projects to be finalized during the entirety of the semester and there were supporting warm-ups, workshops, and discussions along the way. All that being said, I definitely enjoyed the class and the work that I produced, I progressed further and discovered a lot about my own craft. It's not that I found it to a negative experience, I just think a different structure would be more appropriate.
